evidence: ADNI recruits participants aged 55-90 years with memory complaints, mild cognitive impairment, or Alzheimer's disease dementia
ADNI follows participants for 5-10 years with assessments every 6-12 months depending on diagnosis category
CSF biomarkers measured: Aβ42, Aβ40, total-tau, phosphorylated-tau-181
Plasma biomarkers include: plasma Aβ42/40 ratio, p-tau181, p-tau217, NfL, GFAP
MRI protocol includes: T1-weighted MP-RAGE, T2-weighted, FLAIR, and functional sequences
PET imaging uses florbetapir (amyloid), flortaucipir (tau), and FDG (metabolism) tracers
Cognitive batteries include: ADAS-Cog, MMSE, CDR-SB, and FAQ for functional assessment
Memory tests include: Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test and Brief Visuospatial Memory Test
Primary outcome: Alzheimer's disease dementia diagnosis; Secondary: cognitive decline rate
ADNI data organized in tabular CSV files with standardized variable names and visit codes
Visit codes: baseline, month6, month12, year2, year3, year4, year5, etc.
Data access requires ADNI Data Use Agreement and NIH approval
Inclusion requires: CDR 0-2, study partner, MRI-compatible, English speaking
Exclusion: other neurological conditions, significant medical illness, recent imaging
Progression criteria: conversion from MCI to AD dementia documented by ADNI criteria
Three main cohorts: normal cognition (n~200), MCI (n~400), AD dementia (n~200) at baseline
Annual visits for normal and AD dementia; biannual for MCI cohort
Genetic data collected: ApoE genotyping required for all participants
MRI sequences standardized across all sites: 3T scanners with phantom calibration
Progression outcome defined as: CDR increase >=1 point or AD dementia diagnosis
